note: General introduction; Rajgir and Ajanta named only.

author: Mid-eastern Circle, ASI (Rajgir); G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University (Kausambi); K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, V. Mishra (Kumrahar)
name_in_asr: Jivakamravana; Ghoshitarama, Kausambi; Kumrahar, ancient Pataliputra
asr_identification: Jivakamravana at Rajgir (Patna); Ghoshitarama monastery at Kosam (Allahabad); Kumrahar (Patna) = Pataliputra
evidence: Rajgir 1953-54: two building phases of elliptical halls with coarse red ware at the Jivakamravana site; Kausambi: Ghoshitarama (identified 1951) excavated, small stupas, inscription of the nun Buddhamitra of Kanishka's reign, rampart c. 6th c. BC rebuilt thrice; Kumrahar structures from c. 150 BC
quote: The site, of Jivakamravana, where Jivaka, the court-physician of Bimbisara, is believed to have erected a monastery for Buddha was one of the sites chosen for excavation … This year the excavation was concentrated on the site of the Ghoshitarama monastery, identified as such in I951 … at the site of Kumrahar, ancient Pataliputra
note: Jivaka's mango grove (09.02.08): Mizutani places remains close to the E gate of old Rajagrha; the dig is at the site already called Jivakamravana, no inscription; asr/ar empty. Ghoshitarama: the 1951 identification (Sharma) that Mizutani's 05.05.03 follows; against Cunningham's Gopsahsa (asr). Kumrahar = Pataliputra as Mizutani (08.02.01) and AR.

author: University of Saugor, M. G. Dikshit (Sirpur); Dept of Archaeology and Museums, Rajasthan (Bhinmal)
asr_identification: Sirpur (Raipur): 7th-c. capital; Bhinmal (Jodhpur) = Srimala, capital of the Gurjaras
evidence: Sirpur: Saiva panchayatana temple excavated; Bhinmal: medieval brick structures, dark grey and red-polished ware
quote: Sirpur, the capital of the Pandava dynasty of the seventh century, contains the ruins of several medieval temples … Bhinmal, the ancient Srimala, Ratnamala or Pushpa-mala, the capital of the Gurjaras in early medieval times, was excavated
note: Neither site is linked to Xuanzang here. Sirpur as 7th-c. capital supports Mizutani's capital of Kosala (10.12, recent view; epig also Sirpur; asr Cunningham: Chhattisgarh). Bhinmal = Srimala, Gurjara capital agrees with Mizutani's majority view for 11.11 (asr: Balmer, Cunningham).
Conservation (Kausambi, Rajgir, Nalanda, Sarnath, Kasia); no identification.

author: A. Ghosh (DG, general survey of the year)
name_in_asr: Ghoshitarama at Kausambi; Mauryan palace at Pataliputra (Kumrahar); Sirpur
asr_identification: Ghoshitarama, Kosam; Kumrahar (Patna) = Pataliputra; Sirpur (Raipur)
evidence: summary of the year: Ghoshitarama excavation completed with the E gate; Kumrahar Mauryan palace; Buddhist establishment at Sirpur with inscription of Balarjuna (8th c.)
quote: The excavation of the Buddhist establishment of Ghoshitarama at Kausambi was completed, and the remains of the adjacent eastern gateway of the city were exposed … Significant facts about the nature, extent and destruction of the Mauryan palace at Patali-putra were brought to light by the current work at Kumrahar
note: Summary; details in 17 and 19. Agrees with Mizutani (05.05.03, 08.02.01, capital of 10.12 at Sirpur).
Purana Qila and Ahar; Mathura named only.

author: M. Venkataramayya (Northern Circle) and Ballabh Saran (Headquarters), ASI
asr_identification: Katra mound, Mathura = large part of the ancient urban settlement, within a double ring of mud ramparts
evidence: trench 500 ft N of Aurangzeb's mosque on the Katra: natural soil at 42 ft; Period I (6th c. BC) grey wares, Period II NBP ware with ring-wells; two rings of mud ramparts (outer elliptical, inner quadrangular 'citadel')
quote: the recent discovery of the Painted Grey Ware at the vast Katra mound, which represents a large part of the ancient urban settlement, provided additional incentives. Furthermore, an exploratory survey revealed the existence of two rings of mud-ramparts
note: Mizutani: capital = the town of Mathura (04.07). The dig supports Cunningham's Katra mound as the ancient city (asr) against the AR view (ancient Mathura = the high ground SW of the town, not the Katra).

author: D. R. Patil, Mid-eastern Circle (Rajgir); G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University (Kausambi); V. Mishra, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (Kumrahar)
asr_identification: Jivakamravana, Rajgir; Ghoshitarama and E gate at Kosam; Kumrahar = Mauryan pillared hall of Pataliputra
evidence: Rajgir 1954-55: another elliptical structure with two large halls (fig. 4 plan), crude red ware; Kausambi: plan of the Ghoshitarama with massive square stupa, Hariti shrine, S boundary wall 181 ft (Bhadramagha to 6th c.), E gateway with mud-bund curtain; Kumrahar: 84-pillared hall, wooden bases, destroyed mid-2nd c. BC
quote: Renewed excavation at the site of Jivakamravana under Dr. D. R. Patil of the Mid-eastern Circle exposed a few more buildings … the main objectives being the completion of the excavation at the Ghoshitarama monastery and the excavation of the rampart and the eastern gateway
note: Same identifications as 4; no inscription naming either site this year. Mizutani's 05.05.03 (monastery N of the E gate) rests on this work.
Nagarjunakonda excavation; no Xiyu ji identification (Sriparvata not mentioned).

author: M. G. Dikshit, University of Saugar
asr_identification: Sirpur (Raipur): two Buddhist monasteries 1 mile S of the Lakshmana temple
evidence: Main Temple (monastery-temple) built by bhikshu Anandaprabhu in the reign of Balarjuna (c. first quarter 8th c., inscription), occupied c. 200 years, then Saiva; Lower Monastery; local bronze school
quote: The first site yielded the remains of two large Buddhist monasteries adjacent to each other, styled respectively as the Main Temple and the Lower Monastery … According to an inscription the structure was built by one Bhikshu Anandaprabhu in the reign of Balarjuna in about the first quarter of the eighth century
note: No reference to Xuanzang's Kosala; the monasteries are a century after him. Bears on Mizutani's capital of 10.12 at Sirpur (epig also; asr: Cunningham's Chhattisgarh/Maha-Kosala).
Epigraphy (Mathura Kushan inscription, Nagarjunakonda); no location.

author: A. Ghosh (DG, general survey of the year)
name_in_asr: Pataliputra; Ghoshitarama at Kausambi; Kanauj; Sirpur
asr_identification: Pataliputra (Patna city); Ghoshitarama, Kosam; Kanauj; Sirpur
evidence: summary: Pataliputra stratigraphy and fragment of a probable Asokan pillar-capital; Ghoshitarama work wound up with 16 structural sub-periods over a thousand years; Kanauj PGW below NBP; two more monasteries at Sirpur
quote: At Pataliputra, even within the limited areas available for digging, were obtained valuable stratigraphical evidence and antiquities, including the fragment of a probable Asokan pillar-capital … the work in the Ghoshitarama area at Kausambi was wound up with the identification of as many as sixteen structural sub-periods
note: Summary; details in 26 and 28. Agrees with Mizutani throughout.

author: K. K. Sinha, Excavations Branch (Kanauj); G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University (Kausambi); Vijayakanta Mishra, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (Pataliputra)
name_in_asr: Ghoshitarama, Kausambi; ancient city of Kanyakubja; Pataliputra
asr_identification: Ghoshitarama at Kosam: Main Stupa with an Asokan (3rd-c. BC) enlargement = the stupa Xuanzang ascribes to Asoka; Kanauj mound = Kanyakubja; Patna City sites = Pataliputra
evidence: Ghoshitarama: occupation c. 6th c. BC-6th c. AD in 16 phases; Main Stupa built c. 5th c. BC, enlarged in the 3rd c. BC; Bhadramagha's name on a jar; destroyed by the Hunas under Toramana. Kanauj: 40-ft deposit, PGW to late medieval. Pataliputra: NBP period, Mauryan polished pieces, conflagration before 100 BC
quote: The most important of the additions was at the third stage, attributable to the third century B.C. Incidentally, it may be recalled that Hiuen Tsang credits Asoka with the construction of a stupa at Ghoshitarama … at the mound representing the ancient city of Kanyakubja … to bring to light remains of the ancient city of Pataliputra
note: The excavator ties the Asokan stage of the Main Stupa to Xuanzang's Asoka stupa at the Ghosila monastery: supports Mizutani's 05.05.03 (asr: Cunningham put Ghosila's garden at Gopsahsa, rejected). Kanauj = Kanyakubja as Mizutani 05.01; Pataliputra as 08.02.01. The Huna destruction (Toramana) predates Xuanzang, consistent with his ruined Kausambi.
Nagarjunakonda excavation (mula-chaitya inscription); no Xiyu ji place discussed.

author: M. G. Dikshit, Department of Archaeology, Madhya Pradesh
asr_identification: Sirpur (Raipur): habitation-mound, monasteries and fort
evidence: habitation mound: Period I late 5th c. (gold coin of Prasannamatra of Sarabhapura), Period II c. 7th c. with large-scale brick and stone building, Period III 11th c. (Ratnadeva coins); svastika-shaped monastery with 8 ft 6 in Buddha
quote: Period II, dated to about the seventh century, witnessed a large-scale structural activity, attested to by several brick and stone structures
note: Large-scale 7th-century building at Sirpur suits Mizutani's capital of Kosala (10.12) in Xuanzang's time, though the report does not name Kosala or Xuanzang.
Epigraphy; Pataliputra as a family origin in Chandella grants.
Persian inscriptions; Mahaban = a qazi family.
Conservation (Jetavana at Saheth, Sankisa stupa mound and elephant capital, Jivakamravana); no identification argued.
Explorations: NBP ware at Sankisa (ancient Sankasya), Sravasti, Bodh Gaya; no location argued.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: Kosam: encircling rampart (3½ miles) and Ghoshitarama
evidence: 65-ft tower in the E rampart with five phases, rampart earlier than NBP; Ghoshitarama: standing Buddha in local sandstone, balustrade-pillars with Gaja-Lakshmi
quote: primarily to study the nature of the encircling rampart, 3½ miles in perimeter, provided at regular intervals with towers and bastions, and to complete the exposure of the Ghoshitarama area
note: Kausambi = Kosam (Allahabad district) throughout, as Mizutani (05.05: confirmed by Sharma's excavations), the survey (asr: Kosam, Cunningham ASR 01) and AR/epig.

author: A. Ghosh (DG, general survey of the year)
name_in_asr: Kausambi; Vaisali stupa; Rajghat, the site of ancient Varanasi
asr_identification: Kosam defences; relic stupa NW of Vaisali (Basarh); Rajghat = ancient Varanasi
evidence: summary: Kausambi brick wall over 40 ft high; pre-Mauryan stupa at Vaisali possibly one of the eight relic stupas; Rajghat NBP to medieval
quote: At Vaisali was excavated a stupa which had its origin in pre-Mauryan times and may have been, according to the excavator, one of the eight traditional stupas built over the relics of Buddha immediately after his death. Rajghat, the site of ancient Varanasi
note: Summary; Vaisali detail in 54. Rajghat (Varanasi) agrees with Mizutani's Benares (07.01).
Nagarjunakonda citadel and stadium; no Xiyu ji place.

author: A. S. Altekar, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (Vaisali); A. C. Banerji, Mid-eastern Circle (Rajgir)
name_in_asr: stupa built by the Lichchhavis over the relics of Buddha; Jivakamravana
asr_identification: small mound NE of Kharauna-pokhra, c. half a mile NW of Raja-Visal-ka-garh, Vaisali (Basarh, Muzaffarpur) = the Licchavi relic stupa; Jivakamravana area, Rajgir
evidence: excavation guided by Hiuen Tsang's location (NW of the city, SE of the Asoka pillar): mud stupa of NBP date, 25 ft diam., enlarged four times (first in Mauryan times with polished Chunar fragments); soapstone relic casket only a quarter full within a breach in the core; a second breach on the W side; no inscription. Rajgir: more elliptical structures; the long stone wall S of the road to Griddhrakuta is a reservoir bank (Sumagadha?)
quote: The accounts of Hiuen Tsang indicate that during his time the Buddhists of Vaisali believed that the stupa built by the Lichchhavis over the relics of Buddha lay somewhere to the north-west of the city and south-east of the pillar of Asoka … the breach on the western side of the first enlargement (mentioned above) may be ascribed to the post-Asokan ruler who, according to Hiuen Tsang, made an attempt to rifle the stupa
note: The find on which Mizutani's 07.03.03 rests (relic stupa with casket re-buried by Asoka); the excavator is cautious (no inscription). asr: nothing; ar mentions a stupa at Basarh generally. City = Raja-Visal-ka-garh, as Mizutani 07.03 and asr. Rajgir: area already identified as Jivakamravana (09.02.08).
Ratnagiri stupa; Nalanda and Kusinagara cited for the Pratitya-samutpada text.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: Kosam: E gateway defences
evidence: five Periods of the defences; Period I mud wall with brick revetment 42 ft 5 in high (154 courses), pre-NBP sub-periods, NBP in the latest; PGW-like painted grey ware in pre-defence deposit
quote: In the earliest Period, I, the defences consisted of a mud wall with a burnt-brick revetment on the exterior, the latter being available to a height of 42 ft. 5 in. and comprising one hundred and fiftyfour courses of bricks
note: Kausambi = Kosam (Allahabad district) throughout, as Mizutani (05.05: confirmed by Sharma's excavations), the survey (asr: Kosam, Cunningham ASR 01) and AR/epig.

author: A. Ghosh (DG, general survey of the year)
name_in_asr: Sravasti; Kausambi; Vaisali; stupa-site of Amaravati
asr_identification: Sravasti (Mahet); Kosam; Vaisali (Raja-Visal-ka-garh); Amaravati stupa
evidence: summary: PGW and pre-NBP ware in lowest pre-fortification levels at Sravasti; painted NBP at Sravasti and Kausambi; Vaisali defences in three Periods; base of the Amaravati stupa traced and relic-caskets found
quote: Excavation at Sravasti yielded a few speci-mens of the Painted Grey Ware in association with what may be regarded as the immediate predecessor of the Northern Black Polished Ware … At the stupa-site of Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh, despoiled long ago, could still be traced, by excavation, the base of the stupa
note: Summary; Sravasti detail in 76-77, Vaisali in 73. Amaravati stupa = Mizutani's Purvasaila site (10.14.02a); the report does not discuss the identification (AR: Allur for Purvasaila monks).

author: A. S. Altekar and Sita Ram Roy, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute
asr_identification: Raja-Visal-ka-garh, Basarh (Muzaffarpur) = fort of Vaisali
evidence: defences in three Periods: Sunga brick wall on NBP deposit; earthen rampart 68 ft wide dated by a sealing of Agnimitra (2nd c. BC); late Kushan-early Gupta brick rampart with barracks; Gupta sealings inside the fort
quote: Excavation was started by the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, under Dr. A.S. Altekar and Shri Sita Ram Roy at the ruins of the fort of Vaisali, known as Raja-Visal-ka-garh
note: Agrees with Mizutani (07.03, city at Basarh with Raja-Bisal-ka-garh), asr (Cunningham) and ar (Marshall).

author: K. C. Panigrahi and A. C. Banerji, Mid-eastern Circle
asr_identification: Jivakamravana, Rajgir
evidence: another elliptical hall, 228 x 38 ft, rubble in mud-mortar (fig. 6)
quote: in the Jivakamravana area, this year's work by the Mid-eastern Circle of the Department, under Dr. K. C. Panigrahi and Shri A. C. Banerji brought to light another elliptical hall
note: Continues 4, 17, 54; no inscription. Mizutani 09.02.08 (remains near the E gate of old Rajagrha).

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: Kosam: defences
evidence: pre-defence deposits in two sub-periods; Period I of the defences in six sub-periods, NBP first in the uppermost; brick revetment with weep-holes; moat and watch-tower
quote: The earliest Period, I, of the defences was found to comprise six Sub-periods, the uppermost of which was marked by the first occurrence of the Northern Black Polished Ware
note: Kausambi = Kosam (Allahabad district) throughout, as Mizutani (05.05: confirmed by Sharma's excavations), the survey (asr: Kosam, Cunningham ASR 01) and AR/epig.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University (Kausambi); K. K. Sinha, Northern Circle (Sravasti)
asr_identification: Kosam defences; Mahet (Bahraich) = Sravasti
evidence: Kausambi: moat and road at the foot of the rampart, iron before NBP; Sravasti: trench 126 x 15 ft across the N fortification of Mahet; long pre-defence occupation (Period I) with PGW and pre-NBP ware, c. second quarter of 1st millennium BC
quote: EXCAVATION AT SRAVASTI (MAHET), DISTRICT BAHRAICH.—with a view to ascertaining the nature of the fortifications and obtaining a knowledge of the lower levels of the site
note: Mahet = Sravasti as Mizutani (06.01), asr and ar; no new epigraphic evidence (cf. the Jetavana plate in AR).

author: K. K. Sinha, Northern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Mahet = Sravasti (Bahraich)
evidence: Period II c. mid-3rd to mid-1st c. BC (Ayodhya coins, sealing Baladata); early medieval re-occupation, Period III
quote: In the trench in the habitation-area were also encountered deposits yielding typical early medieval pottery, thus signifying the re-occupation of Sravasti for the third time (Period III)
note: Agrees with Mizutani 06.01. Early medieval re-occupation after a gap bears on the ruined state Xuanzang describes, but the report does not say so.

author: A. Ghosh (DG, general survey of the year)
name_in_asr: two stupas adjoining the pillar of Asoka near Vaisali
asr_identification: Kolhua (Bakhra) pillar site, Vaisali
evidence: summary: two stupas by the Asoka pillar excavated, one with pre-Christian relics
quote: Two stupas adjoining the pillar of Asoka near Vaisali were excavated; one of them had interesting pre-Christian relics

author: Sita Ram Roy (with L. A. Narain and B. S. Verma), K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute
name_in_asr: Vaisali: Raja-Visal-ka-garh; pillar of Asoka at Kolhua
asr_identification: Raja-Visal-ka-garh = fort of Vaisali; two mud stupas by the Asoka pillar at Kolhua, 3 miles N of the fort
evidence: fort: brick structures in three Periods, earliest wall pre-Sunga, seals and sealings with Brahmi legends; Kolhua: two mud stupas (183 and 179 ft diam.), the northern with copper vessels, one containing relics 'presumably of a Buddhist saint'; pottery of NBP associations, pre-Christian
quote: Two mounds lying in a north-south row near the pillar of Asoka at Kolhua, 3 miles to the north of the front, respectively measuring 183 and 179 ft. in basal diameter and 25 and 23 ft. in height, were taken up for excavation. Both proved to be mud stupas
note: Kolhua pillar = Mizutani's 07.03.04 (Asoka stupa and pillar); the excavated stupa by the pillar may be Xuanzang's Asoka stupa, but the report does not identify it. asr: Bakhra pillar (Cunningham).
Exploration; Kosambi in Chanda district is a different place.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: Kosam: inner side of the defences
evidence: flank-wall of the gateway complex, rebuilt thrice after construction in the middle of the NBP period
quote: The inner side of the defences was taken up this year for excavation with a view to correlating the rampart and its ancillary structures with the habitation-levels within the city
note: Kausambi = Kosam (Allahabad district) throughout, as Mizutani (05.05: confirmed by Sharma's excavations), the survey (asr: Kosam, Cunningham ASR 01) and AR/epig.

author: Government Epigraphist for India
asr_identification: Amaravati great stupa (Guntur)
evidence: new inscriptions of the 2nd-3rd c. BC; fragment from an Asokan-type polished pillar, perhaps an unknown pillar-edict of Asoka
quote: Some of the inscriptions recently discovered at Amaravati, which can be assigned to the second or third century B.C. on palaeographical grounds, suggest that the celebrated Buddhist stupa of the place was originally built in that age
note: Dates the Amaravati stupa (Mizutani's Purvasaila, 10.14.02a) to the Mauryan age; no discussion of Dhanakataka or Xuanzang.
Museums; Nalanda museum map of the travels of Hiuen Tsang and I-tsing (no location).
Exploration in the Jethian valley (drain compared with Rajgir walls); Sonpur excavation.

author: Sita Ram Roy, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute
asr_identification: Baniya and Lalpura, N and S of Chakramdas, Vaisali area (Muzaffarpur)
evidence: Baniya: three Periods from NBP; Gupta brick shrine; mud stupa near the Chaturmukha-Mahadeva temple over NBP deposit
quote: In one of the trenches, near the Chaturmukha-Mahadeva temple, an earthen heap, resembling a mud stupa, was exposed to a depth of 1.5 metres
note: More early stupa evidence in the Vaisali (Basarh) area; not linked to any of Xuanzang's stupas.
Devnimori excavation; Vadnagar brick size compared.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: stone palace in the SW corner of the walled city of Kosam on the Yamuna
evidence: palace complex 315 x 150 m with tower overlooking the river; stone walls in lime; three phases
quote: brought to light a stone palace. Situated on the bank of the Yamuna, in the south-western corner of the ancient walled city, the palace-complex occupied an area of 315 x 150 metres

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: stone palace in the SW corner of Kosam, possibly king Udayana's
evidence: first-phase rubble walls before NBP, second phase dressed stone, destroyed (sealing of c. 2nd c. BC), third phase brick and stone; origin c. 600 BC
quote: According to the strati-graphic evidence, therefore, the origin of the palace goes back to circa 600 B.C., if not earlier. It is, thus, not unlikely that it was occupied by king Udayana, the renowned contemporary of Buddha
note: Xuanzang puts Udayana's sandalwood image in a great vihara within the old palace of Kausambi (05.05); the report does not cite him, but the excavator's Udayana palace is a candidate for that 'old palace'. Mizutani gives no site for it.
